newsitem.title: USA: US FAA says Taiwan complies with safety standards.
newsitem.headline: US FAA says Taiwan complies with safety standards.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said Friday that Taiwan had been reassessed and now complied with international aviation safety standards.

Taiwan had been rated conditional following an assessment carried out last October. The assessments do not indicate whether individual carriers are safe, rather they determine whether foreign civil aviation authorities are in place and the extent to which they ensure operational and safety procedures are maintained by their carriers, the FAA said.

In Taipei earlier Friday, the Civil Aeronautics Administration said this clearance would mean China Airlines 2610. TW and Evergree Marine unit EVA Airways could operate new routes in the United States.
Under a Feb 28 open skies agreement, Washington would lift curbs on passenger and cargo operations, enabling carriers from Taiwan to fly to any city in the U.S. at will.
China Airlines has applied to operate new cargo flights between Taipei and Anchorage, Alaska, and with the U.S. announcement, is considering adding other routes, airline officials said in Taipei.
EBVA is studying three new routes -- Anchorage, Washington and Chicago, a spokesmen said, adding the airline was reviewing other locations.
The two airlines currently operate flights to San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York and Hawaii.
